# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We as members, contributors, and maintainers pledge to make participation in this
project a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size,
visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity
and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, colour, religion, or sexual
identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming,
diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Our standards

Behaviour that contributes to a positive environment:

- Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
- Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
- Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
- Accepting responsibility, apologising to those affected by our mistakes, and
  learning from the experience
- Focusing on what is best for the community, not just for us as individuals

Behaviour that is unacceptable:

- Sexualised language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
- Public or private harassment
- Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address,
  without their explicit permission
- Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
  professional setting

## A note specific to this project

This is a reverse-engineering project, which means most of what gets discussed
here is somebody being wrong about something in public — including the
maintainers, repeatedly and in writing. The
[history page](docs/10-history.md) and
[pairing page](docs/12-pairing.md) both document conclusions that were confidently
stated and later retracted.

That culture only works if being wrong is cheap. So:

- **"I don't know" and "I was wrong" are good contributions.** They are how the
  hardware validation eventually happened.
- **A question is not a failure of preparation.** If the docs did not answer it,
  that is a bug in the docs.
- **Attack the claim, not the person.** "This control does not distinguish those
  two cases" is useful. "Did you even read the spec" is not.
- **A negative result is a result.** A report that this does *not* work on your
  device is as valuable as one that says it does — arguably more, since the
  evidence base is currently two HomePods.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behaviour may be
reported to the maintainers by opening an issue, or privately via the contact
address on the maintainer's GitHub profile. All complaints will be reviewed and
investigated promptly and fairly.

Maintainers are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of
any incident, and have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject
comments, commits, code, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned
with this Code of Conduct.
